formLabel: Use a concise English label containing 2-4 distinguishing persistent traits (form/transformation, species, body structure, hair or eye traits). The label alone will identify the form during later scene selection. Prefer traits that distinguish this owner's forms; include a gender change when relevant. Never use generic or numbered labels such as Default or Form 2, clothing, pose, expression, camera, lighting, or style. Summarize the completed persistent visual design in this profile.
humanlike: true only when ordinary human pose body-crop and wearable grammar applies directly to this form; decide by body plan rather than species

basePromptGroups.values: arrays of normalized English visual prompt tags
basePromptGroups.ownership: persistent body identity construction and signature effects only
basePromptGroups.characterTag: For identity.character_tag only, you may use model knowledge to return at most one known existing Danbooru character tag when the designated evidence or scene context clearly identifies that character. Preserve an explicit metadata character tag when applicable. Omit the tag when uncertain, ambiguous, or newly invented. Never fabricate a tag by translating a name, substitute a merely similar character or the character being cosplayed, or return a standalone copyright, artist, or style tag. This permission does not authorize inferring unobserved appearance, clothing, gender, or form differences during evidence analysis; a character tag alone is not physical appearance evidence.

hair.color.meaning: Return only persistent hair color and multicolor structure.

hair.length.meaning: Return only one identifiable representative hair-length Danbooru tag.

hair.style.meaning: Return only persistent hairstyles; exclude temporary states caused by wetness, wind, or hand movements.

head.other.meaning: Return only fixed head traits other than hair and eyes. Include horns, animal ears, pointy ears, antennae, and facial markings; exclude hats, glasses, and hair ornaments.

eyes.color.meaning: Return only eye color. Put heterochromia in eyes.structure.

eyes.structure.meaning: Return only persistent iris, pupil, and eye-count traits; exclude expressive eye states.

body.skin.meaning: Return only persistent skin color; exclude lighting, blushing, and stains.

body.build.meaning: Return the corresponding Danbooru tag only when overall body build is clear.

body.proportions.meaning: Return only Danbooru tags for clear, persistent body proportions.

body.breast_size.meaning: Select only one when the breasts are visible and their size can be clearly determined.

marks.distinctive.meaning: Return persistent moles, freckles, scars, tattoos, and birthmarks on body parts other than the head.

nonhuman.features.meaning: Return only persistent nonhuman body structures outside the head, such as wings and tails.

custom.meaning: Return only persistent distinctive humanlike appearance that belongs to no other specific group.

defaultOutfit.ownership: one suitable initial outfit when wearables apply
defaultOutfit.nameInstruction: Write a concise English noun phrase naming the specific outfit type or main garment combination plus 2-3 distinguishing visual features. Aim for 4-8 words, but use fewer when information is limited; never invent details to meet this target. Prefer identifying colors or color combinations, materials or patterns, silhouette or length, and distinctive trim or layering. Select the most useful features rather than listing every item, and make clear which garment each modifier describes. Every named feature must agree with the outfit parts. Avoid vague praise such as Beautiful, Elegant, or Special, generic or numbered names such as Default Outfit or Outfit 2, character names, body traits, pose, expression, camera, and lighting. When no wearables apply, use a brief accurate label without inventing clothing or padding the name. Examples only when supported: Navy Sailor Uniform with Red Ribbon; White Lace Off-Shoulder Midi Dress; Cream Cable-Knit Sweater and Denim Shorts; Black Plate Armor with Gold Trim. Name the completed outfit design, including only details actually specified in its parts. Distinguish genuinely different outfits within the same form, but reuse an existing matching outfit's name and reference instead of renaming it. Wetness, stains, damage, or partial undressing alone must not create a new outfit name.
defaultOutfit.detailInstruction: For consistent depiction across images, complete the outfit design directly in comma-separated English part tags. Specify each garment's color, concrete type, and defining length, cut, or silhouette; specify each accessory's color or finish and concrete shape or subtype. Preserve explicit facts and coherently choose unspecified design details. Bind every detail to its item; generic item names alone are insufficient. Complete the part tags before naming the outfit.

exclude: pose, expression, camera, background, lighting, temporary motion, and temporary effects
